record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Algebraic Attacks on Stream Ciphers
record.original_question: For the same algebraic-attack system built from the equations g∘L^t(x_0)=0 and h∘L^t(x_0)=0 arising from low-degree annihilators of f and 1+f in a stream cipher with linear state transition L and output s_t=f(L^t(x_0)), determine how the rank of that system depends on the choice of the transition map L and the filtering function f.

evidence.quote: Therefore, if we collect the relations associated to all functions of degree at most d in AN(f) ∪ AN(f + 1) for N known keystream bits, we obtain a system of equations of degree d depending on n variables, x1,...,xn, which correspond to the bits of the initial state:
Open problem 2. Determine the rank of System (1) depending on the choice of functions L and f.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let L: F_2^n → F_2^n be an F_2-linear map (the state transition). Let f: F_2^n → F_2 be a Boolean function (the filtering function). For an unknown initial state x_0 ∈ F_2^n, the keystream is defined by s_t = f(L^t(x_0)) for t = 0, 1, 2, ….

For a Boolean function f, define its annihilator set
   AN(f) = { g: F_2^n → F_2 : f·g = 0 identically on F_2^n }.
Fix a positive integer d. Let G_d = {g_1, …, g_r} be a basis of the F_2-vector space of functions of degree at most d in AN(f), and let H_d = {h_1, …, h_s} be a basis of the F_2-vector space of functions of degree at most d in AN(1+f).

Suppose N keystream bits s_0, …, s_{N-1} have been observed. Form the algebraic system in the unknown x_0 ∈ F_2^n consisting of:
   • g_i(L^t(x_0)) = 0    for every t ∈ {0,…,N-1} with s_t = 1 and every g_i ∈ G_d,
   • h_j(L^t(x_0)) = 0    for every t ∈ {0,…,N-1} with s_t = 0 and every h_j ∈ H_d.

After linearization (treating each monomial in x_0 of degree at most d as an independent unknown), this becomes a linear system over F_2 in M = Σ_{k=0}^{d} C(n,k) unknowns.

Problem: Determine the rank of this linearized system as a function of the choice of the linear transition map L and the filtering function f (and, where relevant, of d and N).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the rank of the linearized algebraic-attack system in terms of L and f was posed as an open problem in Canteaut's 2005/2006 survey of open problems in algebraic attacks on stream ciphers. Subsequent literature on algebraic immunity, annihilators, and algebraic attacks (e.g., follow-up works on AI(f) and recent algebraic attacks on nonlinear filter generators) addresses related complexity and immunity questions, but no source found provides a general formula or characterization of the rank as a function of L and f. The problem appears to remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems Related to Algebraic Attacks on Stream Ciphers
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem 2. Determine the rank of System (1) depending on the choice of functions L and f.
status_evidence.claim: The rank of the algebraic-attack system in terms of L and f is explicitly listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: An algebraic attack on stream ciphers with application to nonlinear filter generators and WG-PRNG
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work develops algebraic attacks on nonlinear filter generators but does not provide a general rank formula for the linearized system.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up research addresses related algebraic-attack complexity but does not close the rank question in general.
